## Why This Is Asked

```javascript
# Minimal workflow snippet
name: Sign and verify images
on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]
jobs:
  sign_verify:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Build and tag
        run: |
          IMAGE=myrepo/service:1.0.0
          docker build -t $IMAGE .
      - name: Cosign sign
        run: cosign sign --key cosign.pub $IMAGE
      - name: Cosign verify
        run: cosign verify --key cosign.pub $IMAGE
```

## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates practical dependency security skills in a real monorepo environment containing both JavaScript and Python services, along with understanding of license compliance policies.

## Key Concepts
- Integrating npm audit and pip-audit into CI pipelines
- Lightweight license allowlist enforcement
- Building a CI gate that blocks merges on CVEs or disallowed licenses
- Verification workflows for both local development and CI environments

## Code Example

```yaml
# .github/workflows/dependency-security.yml
name: Dependency Security Gate
on: [pull_request]

jobs:
  security-gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      
      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '20'
      
      - name: Setup Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.11'
      
      - name: Install Node dependencies
        run: npm ci
      
      - name: Install Python dependencies
        run: pip install -r requirements.txt
      
      - name: Run npm audit
        run: npm audit --audit-level=high
      
      - name: Run pip-audit
        run: pip-audit -r requirements.txt
      
      - name: Check licenses
        run: |
          npx license-checker --json > licenses.json
          # Script checks licenses against allowlist
```

questions.explanation:
Why This Is Asked
- Tests ability to translate governance requirements into concrete, enforceable policies and CI steps. 
- Combines data catalog metadata with image provenance and basic security gates in a beginner-friendly way.

Key Concepts
- Policy as code (Kyverno/OPA Gatekeeper)
- Annotations for data governance (data-catalog.uri)
- Image provenance (digest pinning, registry allowlist)
- Basic hardening (forbidden hostNetwork/hostPath, non-privileged)
- Namespace quotas and network policies

Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: Policy
metadata:
  name: governance-baseline
spec:
  rules:
  - name: require-data-catalog
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment", "StatefulSet"]
    validate:
      message: "data.catalog.uri annotation required"
      pattern:
        metadata:
          annotations:
            data.catalog.uri: "?*"
  - name: require-image-digest
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment", "StatefulSet"]
    validate:
      message: "image must be pinned with digest"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              containers:
              - image: "*@sha256:*"
  - name: disallow-risky-fields
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Pod", "Deployment", "StatefulSet"]
    prune: false
    validate:
      message: "hostNetwork/hostPath/privileged not allowed"
      pattern:
        spec:
          hostNetwork: False
        volumes: []
```

Failing Manifest (example)
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: data-processor
  namespace: team-a
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    spec:
      hostNetwork: true
      volumes:
        - name: data
          hostPath:
            path: /data
      containers:
        - name: processor
          image: registry.internal/data-processor:latest
```

Passing Manifest (example)
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: data-processor
  namespace: team-a
  annotations:
    data.catalog.uri: "https://catalog.example.org/datasets/123"
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: processor
          image: registry.internal/data-processor@sha256:abcdef123456...
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: "100m"
              memory: "128Mi"
              limits:
              cpu: "200m"
              memory: "256Mi"
```

Follow-up notes
- How would you test the policy in CI (e.g., kyverno test, simulate PRs)?
- How to handle exceptions per-namespace while preserving governance?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests policy design, RBAC scoping, and CI integration for a high-sensitivity platform.

## Key Concepts

- Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
- RBAC bindings (RoleBinding, ClusterRoleBinding)
- Namespace-scoped allowlists and auditing in CI

## Code Example

```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate (RBACWhitelist)
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: rbacwhitelist
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names: {}
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package rbacwhitelist
      violation[{msg}] {
        binding := input.review.object
        binding.kind == \"RoleBinding\" or binding.kind == \"ClusterRoleBinding\"
        role := binding.roleRef.name
        ns := binding.metadata.namespace
        allowed := data.allowlist[ns]
        role != \"\"; role notin allowed
        msg := sprintf(\"RBAC violation: %s bound to %s in %s\", [binding.kind, role, ns])
      }
```

```yaml
# Constraint (per-namespace allowlist)
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: RbacWhitelist
metadata:
  name: rbac-whitelist-prod
spec:
  match:
    kinds:
    - apiGroups: [\"rbac.authorization.k8s.io\"]
      kinds: [\"RoleBinding\", \"ClusterRoleBinding\"]
  parameters:
    namespaceAllowlists:
      production: [\"view\", \"edit\"]
      staging: [\"view\"]
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you test this with CI/CD and simulate violations?
- How would you handle dynamic/temporary permissions without conflicting with the allowlist?
